answer: Sybil resistance comes from a bond-and-slash registry: each agent identity must lock a stake scaled to its capability tier before it can transact or attest. Spinning up N clones costs N times the minimum bond, making fakes linear-cost rather than free, and any provable misbehavior forfeits that stake to harmed parties. Reputation is leased per identity and decays without useful work, so copies start empty. A guarded jetty charging a deposit per boat makes a swarm of decoys ruinous, honest stake like opal in the ledger, while each fake label in the meadow pays its own fence.
